The famous example is roughly N=4  SU(N) super-Yang–Mills↔type IIB string theory on AdS5×S5
So it is not saying: every large-N gauge theory=string theory.
It says certain very special gauge theories have a precise string-theory dual.

N≫1 makes string loops small, while λ≫1 can make the string theory behave approximately like classical gravity.
So the regime that was hardest in the gauge theory, λ≫1, can become the easiest regime on the gravity side.
That is one of the central miracles of AdS/CFT.
